goals: Mechanistic: quantify partitioning of precipitation into surface runoff, ET, and sub-surface drainage/recharge across the Naches HUC8 and attribute it to elevation-driven forcing and soil texture
Validation: evaluate simulated states/fluxes against in-domain observations (SNOTEL SWE, USGS well WTD) and honestly scope the streamflow-gauge comparison
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (via NLDAS-resolved precip/temperature and snow regime)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column transient ELM natively partitions water into ET, surface runoff, and drainage; spatial sampling across the basin's elevation/soil heterogeneity answers the partitioning question at column scale.

answerable: Column-scale partitioning of P into ET, surface runoff (QOVER), and drainage/recharge (QDRAI)
Basin-scale elevation/climate gradient effect — NLDAS-2 at 12 km resolves orographic precip and the rain-snow transition across 1625 m of relief
Soil-texture control on partitioning via per-column SSURGO
SWE evaluation against the 6 SNOTEL stations (H2OSNO in default output)
WTD evaluation against USGS wells (co-located, with expected 1-D vs lateral-flow bias)

not_answerable.aspect: Streamflow validation against the 93 USGS gauges
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral transport/routing, so it produces no integrated streamflow for gage comparison

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km terrain control on partitioning (ridge/valley contrasts finer than the NLDAS cell)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 12 km forcing has no within-cell lapse rate; sub-grid terrain is unresolved

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x soil-texture classes) with targeted oversampling
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands span the rain->snow forcing gradient that NLDAS resolves; 3 texture classes span the SSURGO range controlling infiltration vs runoff vs drainage. 4x3=12 is the smallest set that crosses both axes; denser gridding adds cost without resolving a new driver.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample valley bottoms/riparian corridors (strongest recharge and shallow-WTD signal) and the 1000-1400 m rain-snow transition (where snowmelt timing drives partitioning shifts). Downstream expander samples DEM+SSURGO to realize points.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light replication (2x) in the rain-snow transition band because partitioning is most sensitive there; single columns elsewhere.

sampling_plan.reason: Low-elevation, rain-dominated columns spanning soil texture — isolates soil control on ET/runoff/recharge where recharge signal is strongest.
Mid-low band bridging rain and transitional snow to capture texture x mild-elevation interaction on partitioning.
Most sensitive zone where snowmelt timing reshapes runoff/recharge split; oversampled for that reason.
High-elevation snow regime end-member for the elevation forcing gradient (accepts 12 km ridgetop SWE underestimation).

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place validation columns at station coords; compare seasonal peak SWE and melt-out timing
co-located — compare warm-started/spun-up ZWT to observed WTD; expect 1-D vs lateral-flow bias, reported as a result
aggregated — NOT natively possible; would require aggregating/routing column runoff to gauge outlets. Flagged as gap, not delivered.

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 baseline forcing, native SSURGO soil, Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.why: Combine independent column runoff into integrated streamflow at gauge outlets
requires_capabilities.blocks: Streamflow validation against the 93 USGS gauges

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS 12 km has no within-cell lapse rate
requires_capabilities.blocks: Resolving sub-12 km terrain control on partitioning

requires_capabilities.capability: WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013) or multi-year spin-up
requires_capabilities.why: Recharge/WTD are slow states; cold start pins water table at ~8.8 m and reads recharge ~0
requires_capabilities.blocks: Meaningful recharge and WTD output and their validation

requires_capabilities.why: Co-locate and compare simulated peak SWE
Co-locate simulated ZWT to observed WTD

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM + SSURGO raster sampling and HUC8 boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: Expand stratification rules into concrete columns

assumptions: Naches is inside CONUS so NLDAS-2 12 km elevation-resolved forcing is available (not Qian fallback).
SSURGO soil coverage exists across the basin for per-column native soil.
Warm-start carrier runs are affordable at ~18 columns; NLDAS costs ~10x Qian.
Recharge is interpreted as ELM sub-surface drainage (QDRAI), acknowledging no lateral groundwater flow.
SNOTEL station coordinates are usable to pin validation columns.
open_questions: How many USGS wells have usable WTD records inside the HUC8, and over what period?
Which forcing years should anchor the analysis (full 1980-2018 climatology vs a representative wet/dry subset)?
Is a routing/aggregation step in scope, or should streamflow be dropped from validation entirely?
Are SNOTEL station elevations high enough that 12 km-cell SWE underestimation will dominate — should those columns be treated as analog rather than strict co-located?
